item.title: MJR Morning Brief — September 24, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Paramount is lining up more financing for its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. The company has launched syndication of a $7.5 billion term loan and says it plans to raise another $44.4 billion in secured debt. The money would help fund the WBD purchase and repay existing debt as Paramount works toward completing the massive media combination.
Here's another story we're following,
Taylor Swift has another big moment planned for Sunday’s MTV Video Music Awards. Her new “Patient Zero” music video, directed by Swift and starring Colin Farrell and Dakota Johnson, will make its world premiere during the show. The VMAs, hosted by Snoop Dogg, air Sunday night on CBS and MTV and stream on Paramount+.
In other media news,
Baltimore has a new sports radio station. WQLL-AM has launched FOX Sports 1370, carrying FOX Sports Radio’s weekday lineup including Dan Patrick, Colin Cowherd and Covino & Rich. The station has also added VSiN for nights and weekends, giving Baltimore sports talk and betting coverage throughout the week.
Turning to another story,
Podcast fans apparently aren’t choosing between audio and video — they’re using both. Acast’s Podcast Pulse 2026 found 78% of fans consume podcasts in multiple formats, and 63% have even started an episode one way and finished it another. The takeaway: where and when people listen may matter more than the format itself.
Also this morning,
Philadelphia’s 92.5 XTU is going all Dolly on September 25. The station is celebrating Dolly Parton Day — with 9/25 serving as a nod to her hit “9 to 5.” XTU will feature Dolly’s music, stories and career highlights throughout the day, with listeners encouraged to add a little kindness and plenty of rhinestones.
Elsewhere in the industry,
TuneIn is headed into more connected cars. Stingray says a new global agreement with Stellantis will bring TuneIn directly into select future vehicles, giving drivers access to more than 100,000 radio stations, plus podcasts, music and news. The companies haven’t yet announced which Stellantis models will get the service.
And in another development,
Sony Music Group is becoming the first music company to join ARIAM, a global coalition promoting responsible artificial intelligence across creative industries. Sony says it will push for AI policies that protect artists and songwriters while supporting innovation, including licensing partnerships between AI companies and rights holders.
Meanwhile,
Houston Public Media is launching a $15.5 million Future Fund to strengthen its long-term financial future following the loss of federal funding. The campaign starts with $1 million from The Cullen Foundation and $100,000 from the Conely Foundation, with funding planned for local journalism, new audiences and additional revenue opportunities.
And finally,
FOX Sports Radio is teaming Stugotz with Chris “The Bear” Fallica for a new college football podcast. “College Football with Stugotz & The Bear” debuts Friday and will drop new episodes Mondays and Fridays throughout the season, combining college football analysis, traditions and plenty of personality.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
